name: jw0799-vault-ios
goal: Prove Harness iOS can sign scoped approvals and seal synthetic entries to the exact runner, then verify physical Face ID and legacy-entry migration.

evidence: The brief requires synthetic-only native interoperability, followed by physical Face ID, cross-UID proof and migration acceptance. Existing fake-phone tests missed that the device queue withheld the public runner key; the strengthened broker test failed on that exact assertion.

title: Verify device-bound Face ID approval and denial on a physical enrolled iPhone.
Prove sealed import, save and reopen of a synthetic legacy entry before cutover.

evidence: Native CryptoKit signs V1 queue reads and V2 decisions. It checks the displayed runner fingerprint before sealing and binds the exact request scope. The authenticated broker queue returns only the public runner key and metadata.

10 tests passed across the broker and macOS-compiled native wire fixture. Browser and API credential delivery, OAuth device grant, denial, wrong key/method, expiry and replay were exercised. Swift iPhone SDK typecheck and project limits passed.

title: Verify the native reviewed legacy storage contract and receipt.

evidence: Swift verified the sealed legacy vector against its reviewed account and login digest. The synthetic fixture reopened the stored entry and refused expiry, changed envelopes and a failed store without returning a receipt. Device-only Keychain and Face ID code passed iPhoneOS SDK typecheck.

title: Verify that only a prepared executor can bind the runner and publish the reviewed request to the inbox.

evidence: The Unix broker rejects missing, wrong-host, altered, expired, replayed or wrong-UID authorizations before inbox publication. The packaged CLI worker checks the real local peer, and the Swift bridge exercises approved and denied synthetic requests with the signed runner binding.
